AcceptanceView.description:
One acceptance condition — what must be measurably true for the task to count as done.

The same shape is both the **input** (`task/create`) and the **view** (what is required), so the card can never show a condition the verifier does not check.

label.description: The human's own wording, when they gave one. Absent = derived from the fields above.

path.description: Path, relative to the task's working directory (an absolute path must land inside it).

pattern.description: Plain substring for `fileContains` — **not** a regex: a badly written pattern must not be able to stall a whole round.

AgentTaskView.description: One task as the human sees it. `status` is a string on the wire (pending / running / suspended / needsAttention / done / failed / cancelled) — the dashboard paints it.

acceptance.description: What must be measurably true. Empty = no objective conditions (single-turn task).

checks.description: The latest verdict per condition, same order as `acceptance`.

currentTurnId.description: The turn currently carrying this task (a heartbeat; absent when idle).

cwd.description: The task's own working directory (the boundary for verification and writes).

goalCondition.description: The goal loop's condition. Absent = a single-turn task: done when the turn is.

lastStopReason.description: Why it stopped last time — the card's footnote, never guessed from the status.

runCount.description: How many times this task has been executed ("执行 3 次").

sessionId.description: Absent = a task that belongs to no conversation.

tier.description: The declared model tier (`fast` / `chat` / `reasoning`); absent = per-turn decision.

ApprovalLogEntry.description: One row of `approval/log`: the complete record of one "ask before running".

outcome.description: One of approved / denied / timeout / voided.

ApprovalLogEntry.title: ApprovalLogEntry

entries.description: Newest first, capped at 100 entries by the server.

ApprovalRequestedNotification.description:
A "may I execute this?" query.

After throwing the question to the client the server **waits** (120 s by default); the answer arrives via `approval/respond`. No reply, timeout, or no approval channel at all — everything is **treated as denied**: default-deny is this feature's foundation, not its edge case.

argsPreview.description: Human-facing action preview: the raw command or an args summary.

expiresInMs.description: How many milliseconds of silence count as a denial.

reason.description: Why the allow rules did not let it through automatically.

requestId.description: Request id within this turn; echo it back verbatim when answering.

tool.description: What wants to run (tool name; currently only `run_command`).

ApprovalRequestedNotification.title: ApprovalRequestedNotification

remember.description: Remember this decision: write the command itself into the allowlist in `<home>/settings.json` (no wildcards — the user approved this command, not this kind).

accepted.description: Is this request still awaiting an answer? False when the reply arrives too late (timed out, or the turn already ended) — the client learns nobody heard its answer.

BudgetView.description: A task's budget. An absent field means that dimension is uncapped.

CheckView.description: One condition's latest measured verdict. Same order as `AgentTaskView.acceptance`.

detail.description: Passed: the evidence ("report.md 12.4 KB"). Failed: the measurement ("report.md 不存在").

label.description: The condition in the human's words ("report.md 里至少有 3 处结论").

keys.description: Fetch only these keys; absent = return everything.

config.description: The full config after writing, so the frontend can replace its local cache outright.

ConnectorStatus.description: One configured connector, as far as the dashboard needs to know: which one, whether it can actually send, and how wide the door is (allowlist size).

allowRecipients.description: How many entries the recipient allowlist has. `0` means nobody — said, not implied.

newFacts.description: How many new facts this batch distilled; 0 means not due yet or nothing surfaced.

DashboardData.description:
Everything the dashboard's first screen needs, fetched in one shot.

It is not the response to any RPC but the payload of the `joy dashboard` HTTP endpoint (`GET /api/data`). **Why it lives in the protocol crate**: the only criterion is that it crosses languages. The browser side type-checks against it, and hand-copying it would drift again — exactly what this whole effort exists to eliminate.

Fields reuse protocol types directly: the dashboard does no second modeling — it is just a view over these data.

connectors.description: Connectors configured on this machine (0.12.0). Read from connectors.json by ops: it is the same file the app-server registered tools from, on the same machine.

connectorsError.description: Why the connector file could not be read, if it could not — the panel shows this instead of silently pretending there are no connectors.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601, millisecond precision. The page shows "when is this data from".

goal.description: The viewed session's goal, when `sessionId` was asked for. Same shape as `goal/set`'s answer — one source of truth, no second modeling.

inbox.description: The connector inbox (0.13.0): newest mail plus how many still wait for a person. Always present (empty when no connector is configured) so the panel needs no branches.

task.description: The viewed session's current task (goal upgraded to a persisted entity), when asked for.

taskArtifacts.description: What that task actually produced: files that exist, with their sizes (0.14). Always present (empty when there is no task), so the card needs no branch to render it.

todos.description: The viewed session's todo sheet, when asked for and non-empty. This is the model's own working sheet (todo_write), shown to the human as the task card.

DashboardData.title: DashboardData

kind.description: What this fact is **about**: `user` / `feedback` / `project` / `reference` / `fact` (fallback). Anything that resists classification lands on `fact`.

query.description: The search query when the verdict is retrieve; null when skipping.

reason.description: The gate's reason (the ≤5-word kind). Present on fail-open so it can be debugged.

GateDecisionKind.description: The retrieval gate's verdict: whether this turn should search memory at all. Joy's hero moment — retrieving everything by default is slow and lets irrelevant memories skew answers.
GateDecisionKind.title: GateDecisionKind

GoalRoundNotification.description: One notification per goal-loop verdict — "why did it run another round" is never guessed.

reason.description: The judge's reason (or the reason for exiting).

GoalRoundNotification.title: GoalRoundNotification

GoalSetParams.description: Parameters for `goal/set`. Empty `condition` = clear the goal.

condition.description: The goal condition (natural language, e.g. "make the tests green"). Empty/absent = clear.

GoalSetParams.title: GoalSetParams

GoalSetResponse.description: Response to `goal/set`: the authoritative state after setting.

active.description: Whether a goal is currently active.

roundsUsed.description: How many rounds this goal has already consumed.

GoalSetResponse.title: GoalSetResponse

path.description: The node names actually traversed, in execution order.

error.description: Error text when the node throws; errors are logged, never rethrown, and the run still finishes normally.

keys.description: Which state keys the node wrote back.

visit.description: Which visit to this node this is (>1 only happens in deliberately designed loops).

GraphRouteKind.description: Whether the triage graph routed this turn as a "quick answer" or a "full lap".
GraphRouteKind.title: GraphRouteKind

InboxItemView.description: One received message, as the panel shows it. `snippet` is a first-line preview; the full body stays in state.db — the dashboard never needs to ship it around.

InboxListView.description: `inbox/list`: what came in, and how much still waits for a person.

InboxReceivedNotification.description: New mail landed in the connector inbox. One knock, no content: the panel pulls the list.

added.description: How many messages this poll added (deduped by uid).

InboxReceivedNotification.title: InboxReceivedNotification

InboxSummarizeParams.description: `inbox/summarize`: the human's "handle these" — turns the unseen mail into one turn. Empty `session_id` means the dedicated `inbox` session.
InboxSummarizeParams.title: InboxSummarizeParams

InboxSummarizeResponse.description: `inbox/summarize`'s answer: how many mails went into the turn (0 = nothing waiting).
InboxSummarizeResponse.title: InboxSummarizeResponse

id.description: null when the id cannot be parsed (e.g. the request itself is bad JSON).

JsonRpcMessage.description: Any frame the server sends back: a response or an error.
JsonRpcMessage.title: JsonRpcMessage

JsonRpcNotification.description: Server-initiated push (on SSE / stdio this is simply frame after frame of events).
JsonRpcNotification.title: JsonRpcNotification

result.description: The concrete shape depends on method; decoders narrow it to the matching `*Response` type themselves.

removed.description: How many were actually deleted. 0 means there was no memory of this subject to begin with.

MemoryListEpisodesResponse.description: The episode list. **No cursor**: `Episodes::recent` only fetches the most recent N by time desc — storage has no notion of offset. Rather than invent an unusable cursor, it honestly returns null.
MemoryListEpisodesResponse.title: MemoryListEpisodesResponse

source.description: Defaults to `user` (said directly by the user). Consolidation passes `consolidation` when distilling from conversations, so the frontend can tell "you told it" from "it summarized itself".

fact.description: The full fact as written, with id — the frontend can insert it directly, no re-query needed.

Message.description:
One message in session history: a row of `chat_log`.

Same conversation, second viewpoint alongside the live stream (`turnStarted` / `textDelta` / `turnCompleted`): the live stream lives only for **this connection** (gone on refresh); this one makes "refresh, switch devices, look back later" possible.

id.description: The chat_log row number. **Also the cursor**: it is `session/messages`' cursor. Row numbers over timestamps: both rows of one turn are written in the same second, so timestamps cannot order them.

meta.description: This turn's telemetry (gate / tools / iterations / model / usage), **present only on assistant rows**.

Message.title: Message

MessageRole.description:
A message's role. A **closed set** — deliberately no "unknown" escape hatch.

If some future `chat_log` really does grow other roles, `session/messages` will **skip** those rows rather than force a value in — so the frontend `switch` can stay exhaustive and "there is a third role to render" shows up at compile time.
MessageRole.title: MessageRole

ModelProfileView.description: A profile's **view**: unlike the stored copy it contains no secret, only where the secret lives.

active.description: Whether this profile is currently active.

keySource.description: Where the credential lives: `keychain` / `file` / `env:VAR` / `memory` / none (local model). **A pointer, not the key itself** — the UI uses it to honestly show "where your key is stored".

vision.description: Whether this profile's model accepts images. `null` = follow the vendor's default model (the catalog row).

ModelProfilesParams.description: Response to `model/profiles`: all configured model profiles + the active one.
ModelProfilesParams.title: ModelProfilesParams

activeId.description: The currently active id (null when nothing is configured).
When the active profile is removed, active is cleared along with it.

ModelRoutesResponse.description: `model/routes`: the routing table as the panel shows it. Always three rows (the tiers are fixed), each maybe pointing at nothing — an empty table is a valid, honest state.

mode.description: `fixed` (default, active profile wins) or `auto` (per-turn tier pick).

ModelRoutesResponse.title: ModelRoutesResponse

ModelRoutesSaveParams.description: `model/routes/save`: write the whole table (no patch semantics — three rows are cheap and "replace the table" cannot leave a half-edited state behind).
ModelRoutesSaveParams.title: ModelRoutesSaveParams

ModelSaveParams.description: Parameters for `model/save`. `provider` is required only when **creating** — passing only `id` + `make_active` means switch.

apiKey.description: The key itself. Absent = keep as-is (changing models or switching never requires re-sending).

keyEnv.description: Use a key from an environment variable (pass a name like `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`): Joy only reads it and never copies it into any file.

makeActive.description: Make it active right after saving (default true — the smoothest on first setup).

vision.description: Whether this model accepts images. Absent = keep the vendor's default (patch semantics, same as `model`); `true` is how "this vendor's default is text-only, but *this* model sees" gets declared at the moment the profile is created.

ModelSaveParams.title: ModelSaveParams

active.description: Whether this profile is currently active.

current.description: The current model after switching (`provider / model`); null when not fully configured.

keyStoredIn.description: Where the credential **actually** landed: `keychain` / `file` / `env:VAR` / `memory` / `none`. Fall back to a plaintext file and say so honestly — never let the user assume the keychain.

RequestId.description:
Request id: JSON-RPC allows a number or a string.

The number arm is `i32`, not `u64`: ts-rs maps `u64` to TypeScript `bigint`, while `JSON.parse` yields `number` — the client receives `1` typed as `bigint`: the kind of bug that never errors but only fails at runtime. Only `i32` crosses language boundaries — the same rule as v2.rs.
RequestId.title: RequestId

RetryNotification.description:
A "retrying now" notice.

Retries are **never silent**: the user sees this message, not an inexplicable long pause.
RetryNotification.title: RetryNotification

RunResponse.description:
The task API's one-shot shape (`POST /api/run`): a whole turn in, one answer out.

Same request body as `turn/start` (`TurnStartParams`), no stream — the HTTP call returns when the turn finishes. Built for programs (CI, cron, another agent), not for a browser: the dashboard keeps SSE, because a person wants to watch the answer arrive.

model.description: The model that actually answered — the visible proof that a tier pin took effect.

routeReason.description: Why this model was chosen (`tier:fast → mini`, `auto:reasoning → ds-r1`); absent = no routing.

RunResponse.title: RunResponse

RunView.description: One execution of a task. A task may run several times; each attempt is its own account.

status.description: running / waiting / suspended / completed / failed / cancelled.

RunView.title: RunView

jobs.description: All jobs sorted by name; an empty array when none was ever registered.

ScheduleStateRow.description: One row of `schedule/list`: a scheduled job's current state (migration 0012).

claimedMinute.description: Non-null = the last run was interrupted; on restart catch_up decides whether to re-run or give up.

lastFiredMinute.description: The last settled trigger minute (the dedup anchor); null if it never ran.

ScheduleStateRow.title: ScheduleStateRow

ServerNotification.description:
The full stream of events for one turn.

`type` is the discriminant — the frontend switches on it, Python uses a pydantic discriminated union. **No failure here should crash the client**: this only describes "what happened".

delta.description: A streaming text delta. Present only when `turn/start` passed `stream: true`.

oneOf.description: Retrying now (rate limit / transient fault): **sent every time**, never silent.
A command is waiting for approval: answer it first, then the turn continues.

argsPreview.description: Human-facing action preview: the raw command or an args summary.

expiresInMs.description: How many milliseconds of silence count as a denial.

reason.description: Why the allow rules did not let it through automatically.

requestId.description: Request id within this turn; echo it back verbatim when answering.

tool.description: What wants to run (tool name; currently only `run_command`).

oneOf.description: One notification per goal-loop verdict — "why did it run another round" is never guessed.

reason.description: The judge's reason (or the reason for exiting).

args.description: The model-supplied arguments; structure depends on the tool.

output.description: The text the tool returned to the model. Failure details live here too — the turn is not aborted.

newFacts.description: How many new facts this batch distilled; 0 means not due yet or nothing surfaced.

visit.description: Which visit to this node this is (>1 only happens in deliberately designed loops).

error.description: Error text when the node throws; errors are logged, never rethrown, and the run still finishes normally.

keys.description: Which state keys the node wrote back.

oneOf.description: A checkpoint is being resumed after crash recovery (finished tools are not re-run).

iterations.description: How many loop iterations are already done (a checkpoint lands at each tool-results boundary).

oneOf.description: A checkpoint is being resumed: startup reconciliation found it unfinished and the loop continues from where it stood (finished tools are not re-run). The human said earlier "keep going until X" by starting the turn — resuming is not the model assigning itself work.

fromIterations.description: How many iterations the checkpoint had already completed.

reason.description: Why it is resuming (`reconcile: crash recovery`, …).

oneOf.description: A checkpoint is abandoned: the human interrupted the turn (or the session moved on) — it will NOT be auto-resumed. Suspended, not silently lost: the ledger says so.

reason.description: Why it was abandoned (`interrupted by user`, …).

oneOf.description: The task behind this turn changed state (created / running / suspended / done…).

sessionId.description: Absent for a task that belongs to no session.

oneOf.description: New mail in the connector inbox (inbound, 0.13.0). A knock — the panel pulls details.

added.description: How many messages this poll added (deduped by uid).

oneOf.description: Boxed: its `TurnMeta` is an order of magnitude bigger than the others, and notifications are built per event and shipped via channels. ts-rs is transparent to `Box<T>`.

ServerNotification.title: ServerNotification

SessionMessagesParams.description:
Read what was said in a session.

**Why it exists**: without it, the conversation on the page lives only in the browser — a refresh erases it. Also the prerequisite for "switch session".

cursor.description: Fetch only messages **older** than this one (paging back through history). Absent = the newest page.

SessionMessagesParams.title: SessionMessagesParams

SessionMessagesResponse.description: Messages with the **newest first** — opposite to the conversation's direction, because "paging back" is the point: take the latest page, then follow `nextCursor` into the past.

nextCursor.description: Present only when older messages exist: pass it as the next cursor. null = the end.

SessionMessagesResponse.title: SessionMessagesResponse

sessionId.description: Generated by the server when absent.

title.description: Session title = the first 60 characters of the first user message.

SessionViewParams.description: Which session to look at — the shared params of the dashboard's per-session reads (`goal/view`, `todo/view`). One field, one shape, no per-method re-modeling.
SessionViewParams.title: SessionViewParams

SettingsPatch.description: The **write patch** for config. Pass only the fields to change; null means leave as-is.

execAllow.description: Whole-table replacement of the allowlist (`JOY_EXEC_ALLOW`) — what "remember this command" writes.

SettingsPatch.title: SettingsPatch

SettingsView.description: The **read view** of config. Fields are deliberately complete and non-optional: reading it yields the full current state.

historyTurns.description: Working-memory sliding window: only the last N turns go into the prompt.

SettingsView.title: SettingsView

SpentView.description: What the task has consumed so far. Always present (zeroes when nothing ran yet).

TaskActionParams.description: `task/suspend|resume|cancel`: address one task and say why (the reason is shown, not dropped).
TaskActionParams.title: TaskActionParams

TaskArtifactsResponse.description: `task/artifacts`: what this task actually produced, newest first.
TaskArtifactsResponse.title: TaskArtifactsResponse

TaskCreateParams.description: `task/create`: **only a human can start a long task** — there is no tool for it.

acceptance.description: How "done" is measured. Empty = the goal/judge decides, as before.

budget.description: Caps on the whole task's spend. Absent dimensions are uncapped.

cwd.description: The working directory this task owns. Absent = the turn's own cwd decides.

goalCondition.description: The goal condition that keeps the loop going. Absent = single-turn task.

sessionId.description: Absent = the task belongs to no session: it can be created and inspected on its own.

tier.description: The model tier this task runs on (`fast` / `chat` / `reasoning`). Absent = decide per turn (auto mode) or use the active profile (fixed mode). A declared tier always wins — "the task picks the model" is the whole point of the tier.

title.description: What this task is, in the human's words — the card's first line.

TaskCreateParams.title: TaskCreateParams

TaskGetParams.description: `task/get`: address one task by id (a session-less task has no other way in).
TaskGetParams.title: TaskGetParams

TaskListResponse.description: Newest first; `active` is the session's newest non-terminal task, when there is one.
TaskListResponse.title: TaskListResponse

TaskRunsResponse.description: `task/runs`: every attempt of one task, newest first.
TaskRunsResponse.title: TaskRunsResponse

TaskUpdatedNotification.description: A task changed state. The event bus folds it into a ping; the hub's `/api/tasks` shows the row.

sessionId.description: Absent for a task that belongs to no session.

TaskUpdatedNotification.title: TaskUpdatedNotification

TaskViewResponse.description: `task/view`: one session's current task (the card on screen).
TaskViewResponse.title: TaskViewResponse

delta.description: A streaming text delta. Present only when `turn/start` passed `stream: true`.

TierRoute.description: One tier's entry in the routing table. `profile_id` absent = "follow the fallback chain" (`reasoning` → `chat` → active, `fast` → `chat` → active), i.e. what the router does anyway.

profileId.description: `null` is a real answer ("follow the chain"), so it is always on the wire — the panel distinguishes "not configured" from "field missing" by reading this, not by guessing.

TierRoute.title: TierRoute

TodoItemView.description: One row of the todo sheet. `status` is the wire form of `TodoStatus` (pending / in_progress / completed / cancelled) — a string, not an enum: the sheet is the model's vocabulary, the dashboard only paints it.

TodoListView.description: The whole sheet as the human sees it. `revision` is the board's monotonic version — the UI can tell "changed" from "refetched" with it.

output.description: The text the tool returned to the model. Failure details live here too — the turn is not aborted.

args.description: The model-supplied arguments; structure depends on the tool.

TurnAttachment.description: One image attached to a turn. `path` is **home-relative** (uploads land in `<home>/uploads/...`); the server reads the bytes and embeds them — the model never sees a path, it sees pixels. Only image files are accepted; other files keep the "path mentioned in text" route.

mediaType.description: Client-provided media type hint; the server trusts the file extension over this.

TurnCheckpointedNotification.description: A checkpoint has been written: this turn's working memory (model thoughts, tool results) is now in state.db — the loop can continue from here after a crash, finished tools are never re-run.

iterations.description: How many loop iterations are already done (a checkpoint lands at each tool-results boundary).

TurnCheckpointedNotification.title: TurnCheckpointedNotification

interrupted.description: false = this turn already finished; nothing was interrupted.

TurnMeta.description: Telemetry for one turn. Persisted into chat_log.meta, so reopening an old session still shows which brain made which decision, not just the final reply.

goalRounds.description: How many rounds this goal has consumed up to this turn. 0 when no goal is set.

goalStatus.description: The goal loop's exit (`continuing` / `satisfied` / `impossible` / `round-limit` / `blocked`). `None` when no goal is set.

graph.description: Null when no graph was involved.

guardHits.description: How many times the loop guard fired this turn (0 = the model never got stuck repeating/alternating tool calls). Zero is normal; non-zero means part of this turn's budget went to spinning in place.

guardNote.description: What the guard told the model when it fired (a human-readable explanation; null otherwise).

interrupted.description: True when this turn was cut short by `turn/interrupt`. Older metas in the DB lack this field — `#[serde(default)]` lets them parse as before.

model.description: The model that actually answered this turn: the small model when the graph routed quick, recorded as-is.

retries.description: How many provider retries happened this turn (rate limits / transient faults). Zero is the norm.

routeReason.description: How this turn's model was chosen (routing, see route.rs): `auto:reasoning → ds-r1` or `fallback: …`. `None` in fixed mode and when the chosen one is already active — the footer stays quiet and only speaks when a choice/fallback actually happened.

usage.description: Token usage for this turn. The historical flaw of only reaching `turnCompleted` without being persisted is fixed: it now lands in chat_log with the meta, so past turns show their cost too.

TurnMeta.title: TurnMeta

TurnResumedNotification.description: A checkpoint is being resumed: startup reconciliation found it unfinished and the loop continues from where it stood (finished tools are not re-run). The human said earlier "keep going until X" by starting the turn — resuming is not the model assigning itself work.

fromIterations.description: How many iterations the checkpoint had already completed.

reason.description: Why it is resuming (`reconcile: crash recovery`, …).

TurnResumedNotification.title: TurnResumedNotification

attachments.description: Images attached to this message, embedded as image content blocks. Requires a vision-capable provider; a missing or unreadable file fails the turn up front.

cwd.description: Working directory for this turn (per-turn override semantics): must be an existing absolute path (fail-closed admission); relative exec commands and relative read_file/list_dir paths resolve against it. Default = process cwd (old behavior).

stream.description: Whether to stream `textDelta` token by token. On for the dashboard, off for scripts.

tier.description: Pin this turn to a model tier (`fast` / `chat` / `reasoning`). Absent = let the server decide (task's declared tier, auto routing, or the active profile — in that order). Machine callers (task API, webhooks) say the tier; the model itself cannot.

TurnSuspendedNotification.description: A checkpoint is abandoned: the human interrupted the turn (or the session moved on) — it will NOT be auto-resumed. Suspended, not silently lost: the ledger says so.

reason.description: Why it was abandoned (`interrupted by user`, …).

TurnSuspendedNotification.title: TurnSuspendedNotification

UsageByModel.description: Response to `usage/summary`: per-model aggregates + totals. In hub mode this is per-user bookkeeping (one home and one state.db per user — the ledger is isolated by person by construction).
UsageByModel.title: UsageByModel
